title: Mitochondrial Eve
blurb: The woman whose mitochondrial DNA descends unbroken, mother to daughter, to every living human. She was not alone, and she was not the first — she is simply the one whose line never broke.

title: L0
blurb: The first split in the maternal tree. L0 goes one way, everyone else the other.

title: L0d
blurb: Khoisan-speaking southern Africa. Some of the deepest maternal ancestry alive.

title: L1
blurb: Central African rainforest.

title: L1c
blurb: Carried by Central African hunter-gatherer communities.

title: L5
blurb: Rare, East African, very old.

title: L2
blurb: West and Central Africa — and later, through the Atlantic slave trade, one of the most common maternal lineages in the Americas.

title: L2a (Bantu expansion)
blurb: Travelled with farming communities across Central and southern Africa.

title: L3
blurb: East Africa. Every maternal line outside Africa — all of them — descends from L3. The exit was narrow.

title: M
blurb: The southern coastal route: around Arabia, along the Indian Ocean rim, and onward east.

title: M1
blurb: A back-migration — this branch returns to Africa.

title: M7
blurb: East Asia.

title: Q
blurb: New Guinea. Arrived early, stayed put.

title: D4
blurb: Northeast Asia and the Siberian steppe.

title: D1 (Beringia)
blurb: One of the five founding maternal lineages of the Americas.

title: D1 (South America)
blurb: Down the Pacific coast and into the Andes.

title: N
blurb: The other exit branch — north and west out of Arabia.

title: S · O (Australia)
blurb: Australia's founding maternal lineages, isolated for over forty thousand years.

title: X
blurb: Near East and Europe — and, puzzlingly, a small presence in northeastern North America.

title: A
blurb: Northeast Asia.

title: A2 (Beringia)
blurb: Another of the American founding lineages.

title: A2 (Mesoamerica)
blurb: Still the most common maternal lineage across much of Mexico and Central America.

title: R
blurb: The branch that becomes most of western Eurasia.

title: B
blurb: East Asia.

title: B4 (Austronesian)
blurb: The maternal signature of the Pacific expansion, traceable from Taiwan to Polynesia.

title: B4 (Polynesia)
blurb: Carried across a third of the planet's surface in outrigger canoes.

title: B2 (South America)
blurb: An American founding lineage, strongest along the Pacific coast.

title: F
blurb: Mainland Southeast Asia.

title: U
blurb: One of the oldest western Eurasian maternal branches.

title: U5
blurb: The lineage of Europe's Ice Age hunter-gatherers — the people who painted Lascaux.

title: U5 (post-glacial)
blurb: Follows the retreating ice north. Still around 10% of Europeans, a direct maternal thread to the foragers.

title: U6
blurb: North Africa.

title: K
blurb: A younger branch of U.

title: K (first farmers)
blurb: Carried into Europe by Anatolian farming communities.

title: HV
blurb: The Near East, before farming.

title: H
blurb: Would become the most common maternal lineage in Europe — around 40% of Europeans today.

title: H (Europe)
blurb: Spreads with the post-glacial recolonisation and again with farming.

title: JT
blurb: Near East.

title: J
blurb: Strongly associated with the spread of agriculture into Europe.

title: T
blurb: Anatolia and the Fertile Crescent.
